name: hyp-38-half
comment: HALF THE {3,8} TRIANGLE, and a test of the parity argument that explains {3,7}. Eight triangles meet at every {3,8} vertex, so each corner is 45 degrees; an altitude cuts one into a scalene 22.5-90-45 triangle. Chiral, three edge types, the {3,8} edge exactly twice the half-edge. D=16 because 22.5 = 2pi/16; the angles are [1,4,2] and sum to 7 against the 8 a flat triangle would, so the deficit is 1 unit = 22.5 degrees, the tile's area. THE PREDICTION: on {3,7} nothing exists below k=6, because each half-triangle's corner at a vertex is flanked by one FULL edge and one HALF-edge, the two kinds must alternate round the vertex, and 7 is odd — so no {3,7} vertex can be left entirely uncut. Eight is EVEN, so the alternation closes and an uncut {3,8} vertex is allowed. If the argument is right this board has tilings at low k where {3,7} had none, and the alphabet must contain a vertex configuration of eight base corners.
